name: Davi Ousseini-Brătianu
location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone, sleeping in a rotating series of squats; works primarily along the Blackpipe Corridor
description: Davi is slight and quick, the kind of person who seems to occupy less space than his dimensions suggest — useful when you're tagging corponation infrastructure at three in the morning. He has his mother's Nigerien cheekbones and his father's Romanian pallor, a combination that gives his face an angular quality that reads differently in different lights. His hair is grown out into a soft cloud he's bleached pale gold; he's got cat ears installed — small, tufted, matte black — that he paid for with three months of odd jobs and wears with the slightly self-conscious pride of someone whose first big purchase was purely for joy. His clothes are perpetually paint-stained in colors that don't match what he's currently working on.

core_fears: Being disappeared by Ferrogate Transit security for the mural he painted over their substation last month
Becoming ordinary — getting a job, getting tired, stopping
core_desires: To make something so big and so undeniable that it cannot be removed or ignored
To find his father, who left for the Menomonee Gulch labor yards when Davi was eleven and stopped sending messages
coping_mechanisms: Working through the night until exhaustion shuts the anxiety down
Turning fear into aesthetic — his best pieces come from his worst weeks
blind_spots: He believes his youth protects him in a way it fundamentally does not
He mistakes being seen for being understood
psychology.secret: He found his father's last known location two years ago — alive, in a Ferrogate Transit labor contract in the Gulch. He hasn't gone to find him because he doesn't know what to do if the man doesn't want to be found.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Quick and vernacular, Zone slang layered over occasional flashes of careful precision when talking about technique
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast, then suddenly stops; runs sentences together when excited
verbal_tics: 'Nah, listen—' when he's about to make a point
example_lines: 'Nah, listen, the neon isn't the piece, the neon is what the piece is dreaming about, you understand?'
'It's fine. Security rotation is thirty-two minutes, I've counted. It's fine.'

story_hooks: One of his recent murals on the Blackpipe Corridor was painted over within hours — the only murals that get removed that fast are the ones that accidentally documented something
A Tessera corporate art scout has been photographing his work and he's been offered a meeting — the crew thinks it's a sellout, he's not sure what he thinks
narrative_function: Street-level information source about the Zone and the Corridor; local color; potential unwitting witness to things painted over; his escalating ambitions could pull him into danger
augmentations: Cosmetic cat ears (matte black, tufted); no other augmentations — he can't afford them and is mildly suspicious of corporate implant supply chains
daily_life: Sleeps until noon, scavenges or trades for materials in the afternoon, scouts locations at dusk, works at night when the Corridor's security patrols are thinnest.
affiliation: Highland Park Autonomous Zone; loosely affiliated with a graffiti crew called Crow Voltage

decision_rules: Don't tag residential walls — only corporate and transit infrastructure
Never give up a crew member's name, ever, to anyone
escalation_ladder: Runs — and then comes back later to finish what he started

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Bouncy and deflecting, performs confidence he doesn't entirely feel
interpersonal_modes.friends: Loyal to a fault, shares everything, takes up causes on their behalf with more energy than wisdom

stress_responses.low: Talks faster and makes more jokes
stress_responses.medium: Gets very quiet and starts drawing in his margins obsessively
stress_responses.high: Disappears for two or three days and comes back with a new piece somewhere impossible

contradictions: He insists his work is political and for everyone but is privately devastated when people don't recognize his specific aesthetic signature
habits: Leaves small spray-painted offerings to the E.L.F. he calls Spilllight at the base of every major piece
Keeps a physical sketchbook of every tag he's ever done with the date and location
breaking_points: Watching security whitewash one of his murals in real time
Someone claiming credit for Crow Voltage work they didn't do

timeline.event: 2181 — Born in Highland Park to a Nigerien mother and Romanian father
2192 — Father leaves for Ferrogate Transit labor contract in Menomonee Gulch
2195 — First significant tag appears on a Ferrogate substation; joins Crow Voltage
2198 — Locates father's last known address; does not go
2200 — The Blackpipe Corridor murals begin drawing outside attention
